recognize_zh: 腦脊髓液細胞離心片中有多顆空泡狀巨噬細胞：B 細胞內含金黃色菱形結晶（血晶/hematoidin 類結晶），A 與 C 細胞含黑藍色含鐵血黃素顆粒（siderophage），背景有嗜中性球，提示先前出血而非單純穿刺造成的新鮮血。
features: Macrophage (B) containing a refractile golden-yellow rhomboid crystal, consistent with hematin/hematoidin crystal
Macrophages (A, C) with vacuolated cytoplasm containing coarse dark blue-black hemosiderin granules (siderophages)
Macrophage A with an eccentric reniform nucleus and phagocytic vacuoles
Several segmented neutrophils and an occasional lymphocyte in the background
Background of numerous red cell ghosts consistent with hemorrhagic CSF
describe_en: Cytospin of cerebrospinal fluid shows a mixed cell population with increased macrophages among neutrophils and occasional lymphocytes on a background of abundant red cells. Several macrophages are vacuolated and contain coarse dark hemosiderin granules (siderophages, A and C), and one macrophage contains a golden-yellow rhomboid crystal (B), consistent with a hematin/hematoidin-type crystal. These findings indicate breakdown of red cells over days and are not expected from a traumatic tap alone. Findings are consistent with subacute to chronic hemorrhage into the CSF.

ddx.vs: A traumatic tap shows fresh red cells without erythrophages, siderophages or hematoidin crystals, and red cell counts decrease across sequential tubes.
Melanin is brown-black fine pigment that is Prussian blue negative, often with atypical melanoma cells, whereas hemosiderin is Prussian blue positive.
Hematoidin crystals are bright golden-yellow rhomboid or needle forms within macrophages and are iron-negative, unlike colorless extracellular contaminant crystals.
Meningitis shows predominant neutrophils with possible intracellular organisms and low CSF glucose, without prominent pigment-laden macrophages.
